input.brief: EventPilot celebration and event planning assistant for weddings, birthdays and festivals

direction.name: The page is the object
direction.idea: Find the printed or physical artefact that already exists in the subject's world and build the page as that thing. A wedding site is the invitation card. A restaurant is its menu. A conference is the ticket; a record is its sleeve; a shop is the receipt or the swing tag; an archive is a stack of tabbed folders; a course is the syllabus sheet. The artefact supplies everything a template would otherwise invent: its proportions, its typographic manners, its way of grouping information. Visitors recognise the object instantly, which is why these pages feel specific.
direction.composition: The first screen shows the artefact as a single filled panel (paper colour on a contrasting ground) centred or offset, with believable proportions: a card at 5:7, a ticket at about 2.2:1 with a notch cut by `clip-path`, a menu as a tall sheet. All primary content lives on it, set the way that object is set: centred and symmetrical for an invitation, in tidy aligned columns for a menu or ticket. The ground behind is a flat colour or one full-bleed photograph. As the page continues, each section is another piece of the same stationery: a second card, a tear-off stub, a folded panel, always filled shapes with real edges (straight, notched, scalloped, perforated by a dotted `border` of round dots at 4px or more), never outlined boxes. The footer is the back of the object.
direction.typography: Take the manners of the artefact: a bookish serif with small caps avoided, or a blunt condensed face for tickets and posters. Sizes stay within what print would use relative to the panel; the name is large on the panel, details are small and exact.
direction.colour: Paper and ink plus the ground the paper sits on. Two or three flat colours in total, like a two-colour print job.
direction.imagery: Optional. One photograph behind the object, or small photographs placed on it like tipped-in plates. The object itself is the image.
direction.richness: Recognition. The shaped edges, the print-like alignment and the limited inks make a familiar object out of plain HTML.
direction.pitfalls: Choose an artefact that truly belongs to the subject, or it becomes costume. Shape the edges with fills and `clip-path`; an outlined rectangle with a thin border is not an object. Keep text sizes readable on a phone, where the object becomes full width with its shaped edge kept at top and bottom.

hero.name: Card over a dim room
hero.blueprint: A full-bleed, low-key photograph of the room fills the viewport, darkened with `filter: brightness(0.7)` so it reads as atmosphere. Centred over it is one square-cornered panel in a flat warm tone taken from the photograph: columns 4–10, about 55% of the width and 62% of the height, a filled programme card with 32px padding. Along its top edge the three words of the title are spread to the left, centre and right in bold condensed capitals at clamp(28px, 2.5vw, 38px); that line is the headline. Under it sit two left-aligned blocks in the same face and size, line-height 1.0: the facts (date, time, place) as three short lines, then one supporting sentence held to 30ch. Along the card's bottom edge: a credit at left in 14px, the single action as a solid rectangular button in the centre, one text link at right. There is no navigation outside the card. The card is `position: sticky`: as the page scrolls it shrinks with `transform: scale` toward the bottom-left corner and stays there as a ticket-sized stub while photographs of differing sizes pass on a flat ground.
hero.mobile: The photograph fills 100svh and the card sits centred at full width minus 16px margins, 70svh tall. The title words stack as a two-line heading at 9vw at the card's top-left. The facts and the supporting sentence follow at 5.2vw in the condensed face. The action button spans the card's bottom edge. On scroll the card shrinks to a 120px stub pinned bottom-left.
hero.headline: The event or venue name, three words at most and up to about 8 characters each, spread across the card's top edge; two lines on a phone.

motion.name: Pinned story
motion.description: One element holds its place with `position: sticky` (a title, a frame, a product fragment) while the items that belong to it scroll past or swap inside it. The page's ordinary scrolling does the work; nothing is hijacked. Hold it for about one screen per step and three screens at most, two held stages per page at most, with a line of text on every held screen. Recipe: 'Pinned story' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Stacking colour sheets
sections.blueprint: Three to five capabilities, each a full-width flat colour sheet about 86svh tall with only its top corners rounded at 28px. Every sheet is position: sticky, with top offsets rising by 72px from one sheet to the next, so each new sheet slides up over the last and leaves the previous sheet's title band showing, like tabbed folders in a drawer. Inside a sheet: the capability name top-left at clamp(28px, 3vw, 44px), sitting within that 72px band; a paragraph of up to 40ch at 18px bottom-left; and in columns 7–12 one photograph filling the sheet from below the band to the bottom edge, square corners, no inset. Sheet colours follow the palette in a fixed order, with ink chosen per sheet. The heading, two to four words at clamp(40px, 5vw, 80px), sits on the ground above the stack with 48px beneath and scrolls away normally.
sections.mobile: Sheets stay sticky but the offset shrinks to 52px and the name drops to 22px so it fits the visible band. Inside each sheet the photograph comes first at 4:3 and full width, then the paragraph at 17px with 20px padding. Sheets are as tall as their content, 70svh at least.

sections.name: Output slips along the edge
sections.blueprint: For subjects whose result is a piece of text or paper: a receipt, a note, a ticket, a written line. A full-bleed photograph, 100vw by 96svh, sets the scene. In the upper centre, left-aligned in a column starting at 18% of the width, two short paragraphs in paper colour at 28–32px, the first opening with the heading's two to four words; a neutral scrim sits behind that column only. Along the bottom, six paper-coloured slips stand side by side across the full width with 12px gaps, each a filled rectangle of a different height (between 26 and 44svh), their lower ends cut off by the section's bottom edge. Two or three of the slips, not all, are tilted by 1–2 degrees. Each slip carries a sample of real output in the text face at 15px: a bold first line, a divider made of typed characters, then four to eight lines.
sections.mobile: The photograph is 100svh. The paragraphs sit in the top third at 22px. Only three slips show, each 30vw wide, standing along the bottom at different heights, and the row scrolls sideways to reveal the rest. Slip text stays at 14px; do not scale it down.

sections.name: Drag row of moments
sections.blueprint: A story told left to right. Top row: the heading, two to four words at 28–36px, at the left margin; at the right margin two solid square buttons, 48px each, for back and forward. Directly beneath, a solid bar 6px tall spans the full width in a soft tone, with a full-ink segment showing how far the row has been scrolled. Then the row itself: six to nine columns, each 280px wide with 32px gaps, in a horizontally scrolling flex container with scroll-snap that bleeds off both viewport edges. Every column reads top to bottom: a one-line caption at 18px bold that carries the order in words ('We met', 'Two winters on', 'The move'), three lines at 15px in the soft ink, then 80–140px of empty space that varies per column, then a 4:5 portrait photograph. Because the spaces vary, the photographs' top edges rise and fall along the row.
sections.mobile: Columns are 72vw wide with 16px gaps, so the next one always shows at the right edge. The buttons are dropped; the 6px progress bar stays under the heading. The empty space inside columns shrinks to 32–64px but still varies from column to column.

sections.name: The printed guest list
sections.blueprint: Names are printed on a card, the way a programme lists its patrons or an invitation its hosts. On a contrasting flat ground, a paper-coloured panel about 56% of the viewport wide with 5:7 proportions sits centred and rotated by one or two degrees; the section is shorter than the card and clips it with `overflow: hidden`, so the card is cut by the bottom edge rather than framed whole. Inside, 56px padding. At the top, a centred heading of two to four words at 28px. Below it the names run as centred lines at 20–22px with leading 1.7, several names to a line, separated by middots with a non-breaking space either side. One photograph may be tipped in between the heading and the names: 16:9, the full inner width, square corners. The card is a plain filled shape with no outline.
sections.mobile: The card becomes 92% of the screen wide, keeps a one-degree tilt and is still cut off by the section's bottom edge. Heading at 22px, names at 17px with two names to a line. Padding drops to 28px, and the tipped-in photograph keeps the full inner width.

sections.name: Answers as reading text
sections.blueprint: The questions and answers are set as continuous reading text, like the notes at the back of a programme. A heading of two or three words at 28–32px sits in columns 1–3, top-aligned. Columns 5–12 hold the text in two columns (`columns: 2; column-gap: 56px`), each about 36ch wide, at 16–17px with leading 1.55. Each item is one paragraph: the question is the opening run-in, set in the medium weight in the full ink and ending with its question mark, and the answer continues on the same line in the regular weight. Paragraphs are separated by 20px and carry `break-inside: avoid` so none splits across columns. No toggles, no icons, no boxes. Eight to fourteen items fit on one screen, which is the point: everything is answered at a glance. Where the page's reading column is narrow, use one column.
sections.mobile: One column at 16px with 20px margins. The heading leads at 24px. Each paragraph keeps its run-in question in the medium weight, with 18px between paragraphs. The section may run to two screens; do not collapse it into an accordion.

sections.name: The reply card
sections.blueprint: The invitation to act is a printed card lying on the page. On a dark or strongly coloured flat field about 80svh tall, a paper-coloured panel 44vw wide with 7:5 proportions sits in columns 6–12, rotated two degrees, with its lower edge hanging 60px past the section's bottom so the section crops it. On the card, with 48px padding, everything is centred the way stationery is: a heading of two to four words at 32px, one or two lines at 17px, then the action as a solid bar across the card's full inner width, 56px tall, in the ink colour with paper-coloured text. Columns 1–4 hold only a short paragraph at 20–24px in the field's light ink, bottom-aligned 64px above the edge. The card is a plain filled rectangle with square corners and no outline; its rotation and crop make it an object.
sections.mobile: The paragraph comes first at 20px. The card follows at 90% width, tilted one degree, centred, its bottom edge still cropped by the section. Heading at 24px, lines at 16px, and the action bar 52px tall across the full inner width of the card.

references.name: Mosby’s Files
references.idea: An archive of architects presented as a physical stack of coloured index-tab file folders that you flip through.
references.hero: Charcoal background. A slim top bar over a hairline holds the condensed wordmark dead centre and one mono link far right. The headline is one centred line of heavy condensed uppercase at 10vw, about 71% of the width, in the upper quarter. Beneath it, a three-line centred serif paragraph in mid-grey, about 42% wide. From 51% down sits a stack of file folders 86% of the viewport wide: each is a flat colour band with one to three trapezoid tabs rising from its top-left edge, each tab a different colour holding a serif name. Mono category labels sit right-aligned. The front red folder is open, running off the bottom.
references.type: Founders Grotesk bold condensed uppercase at 144px for the title and wordmark; Signifier serif at about 22px for the intro and 28px for tab names; IBM Plex Mono 12px for labels and body. Three unrelated faces, each with one job, and a twelve-to-one size jump.
references.colour: #191919 #d71e1e #1e4bd7 #0c7866 #581e70 #ffe927 — Charcoal ground with five flat poster primaries assigned to folders and tabs; each tab deliberately differs from the folder behind it. No tints, gradients or photos; white type except black on yellow.
references.imagery: No photographs on the index. The folder shapes are the imagery, plus a row of seven small white line-drawn north-arrow and compass symbols and a drawing scale bar borrowed from architectural plans.
references.layout: Centred title block over an 86%-wide folder stack with equal dark margins. Folders overlap at a fixed 60px step so only the tab rows show; the open folder expands into a tall single-colour panel with mono text top-left and plan symbols near the bottom. Under two screens.

sections.description: Four full-width colour bands stacked with a 60px reveal, each with trapezoid tabs growing from its top-left edge. Tabs are about 44px tall with S-curved shoulders, sit side by side with small gaps, and each takes a contrasting flat colour: yellow and black tabs on a green folder, red and blue on purple. Names are white serif at 28px inside the tabs. A mono category label with a small chevron is right-aligned in each band's visible strip.

The front folder opens into a solid red panel nearly two viewports tall. Top-right: its mono category label with a down chevron. Top-left, inset about 60px: a four-line mono paragraph in white, at most half the panel wide. The middle is left empty. Near the bottom, a centred row of seven small white plan symbols evenly spaced; beneath, a baseline row with a drawing scale bar left, year centre, credit and round logo right.

steal: Build navigation as stacked full-width colour bands with trapezoid tabs, each tab coloured to clash with the folder behind it.
Pair a heavy condensed grotesk title with a bookish serif for names and a mono for metadata, giving each face exactly one role.
Borrow notation from the subject's own documents (scale bars, north arrows) as footer ornament instead of generic icons.
references.media: The hero has no picture: its visual weight is a CSS stack of overlapping flat colour folders with sloped tabs covering the lower half of the fold (about 42% of the area), which doubles as the index; an open folder expands to 80vh as the content panel. The only drawings are seven small white plan symbols and a scale bar; no photographs or video on the index.
references.motion: A short entrance: readable at about 1.2s, with 17 title letter spans already in place, and settled by 2.5s as the stack rises about 13px into place and the subline fades up. Lenis on a page only 1.6 screens tall; the header slides away on scroll, and folders and tabs move on one house curve, cubic-bezier(.33,1,.68,1), at 0.65s, with the quicker moves at exactly half that, 0.325s.

references.name: Le Petit Bleu
references.idea: The cafe's teal-and-white stripes become the whole system: one teal ink on cream, everything boxed in thin double outlines like printed menu cards, beside a permanently visible photo of the room.
references.hero: Viewport split 50/50 with 12px gaps. Left: a cream panel with a thin pale-teal outline and rounded corners. Inside, a second outlined box is the nav bar: two-line hamburger left, teal brush-script logo about 300px wide centred, a caps order link right. Below, a two-line light serif headline at about 3.5vw, centred, in teal, then two centred stacks, each a bold caps label, a serif line and a solid teal button wrapped in a second thin outline. Right: a full-height rounded photo of a striped booth, with an outlined hours bar across its top, three slide dots bottom-left and a white address card bottom-right.
references.type: Self Modern, a light bookish serif, for headline and 15px body; Matter SQ bold caps for labels and buttons; Archive Mono Pro typewriter caps for menu rows; a brush-script logo. Section titles are tall condensed serif caps sized so four to seven letters fill the column.
references.colour: #fcfbf7 #13a7b2 #058599 #cfe5e7 #e9b81f — Cream paper and a single teal used for every word, rule, outline and button; no black anywhere. Yellow, floral reds and marble enter only through the interior photographs.
references.imagery: Bright, saturated interior and food photographs; the right-hand panel is a full-height slideshow with rounded corners. Small food shots sit in a horizontal strip, and a fine line drawing of the shopfront with one teal awning fills a card.
references.layout: The left half scrolls as a stack of outlined cream cards (full-width or two-up) with 12px gaps while the right half stays fixed. Card contents are centred. A sticky nav card rides over the stack. On mobile the photo becomes the hero card's background.

sections.description: A card containing only the section word in tall condensed serif caps, teal, sized so its four letters fill the column edge to edge. Below it, a stack of full-width outlined rows about 36px high, each with a category name in typewriter mono caps at left and a thin plus sign at right, separated by 6px gaps. Above the title: a ticker row of tiny caps and a strip of four small food photos with rounded corners.

The same giant condensed title treatment, then centred serif paragraphs in teal with underlined links in a narrow measure of about 280px. Further down, a landscape photo of the two proprietors with a centred two-line caption in tiny sans, followed by more centred paragraphs. All of it lives in the left half while the right photo panel has advanced to a shelf-wall image.

A header row with a tiny bold caps label at left and a script follow-us link with arrow at right, then three portrait images (about 3:5) with 12px rounded corners in a row, the third cropped by the column edge to imply a carousel. Directly below, the next giant section title begins and is cropped by the viewport.

steal: Print everything in one brand ink on cream, including body text, rules and buttons, and let photographs supply the other colours.
Wrap buttons and panels in a second thin outline offset by a few pixels to get a printed-ticket feel.
Keep a tall photo panel fixed on one half and scroll a stack of cards on the other, swapping the photo as sections change.

references.name: Select26
references.idea: A database conference dressed as terminal output: pixel-mono lettering in highlighted cells, a live band of ASCII glyph animation, and one-bit dithered speaker portraits.
references.hero: Near-black page with 96px side margins and about 125px of empty space at the top. Three columns start on one line: at left the event name stacked in three rows of pixel-mono caps, each letter in its own filled cell (green, mint, white); at 36% a two-line description, a small green down-arrow, then date and address in grey; at 66% the ticket terms and an outlined mono-caps button. Below, a full-bleed band about 320px tall of animated glyphs: four rows of large mint and cream hex characters, a block of ASCII shading, a small symbol cluster. A plain section label and the tops of six portraits close the viewport.
references.type: departureMono (pixel mono) at only 34px for the wordmark and for button and table labels; Inter 14-18px with tight tracking for everything else; Manrope minor. Largest live text is 2.8vw: scale comes from the canvas glyphs, not from headings.
references.colour: #0b0e0d #95e5b8 #3ecf8e #e6fbd0 #ffffff #8b908d — One near-black field for the entire page. Three greens (brand green, mint, pale lime-cream) appear only in the wordmark cells, canvas glyphs, links and outlined buttons; all copy is white or grey.
references.imagery: Canvas-drawn ASCII and hex glyph fields in green tints; speaker headshots converted to coarse black-and-white dither, square-cornered, about 4:5, in a strict six-column grid with small name and role captions beneath.
references.layout: Fixed 96px side margins and one six-column grid: info columns, portraits, agenda table and sponsor tiles all snap to it. Sections are separated by space only, with small plain-sans headings; glyph bands at top and bottom bracket the page.

sections.description: A plain 22px sans label, then a six-column grid of portrait tiles with 18px gutters running more than six rows. Every photo has the same 4:5 crop and is rendered as a black-and-white bitmap dither, so mixed-quality headshots look uniform. Beneath each: name in small white sans and role in grey, two or three lines, left-aligned. A leftover final tile sits alone at the left rather than being centred.

The agenda heading reads as a sentence: the section word, a green arrow, then two text tabs, the active one underlined in green. Below, a three-column table: time ranges in small grey mono, session title in white sans, speakers in smaller white on two lines. Column headers are tiny mono caps over one hairline; rows are separated by space, with a single dotted line marking lunch.

The cell-highlighted wordmark repeats at small size above three grey lines and a three-state theme switch made of tiny square icons; an outlined mono button sits far right. Beneath, a full-width band of bracketed hex strings in mixed green fills, some characters inverted in solid cells, with a ticker line of digits running off both edges.

steal: Set each letter of a wordmark in its own filled monospace cell, varying the fill tint per row.
Dither all headshots to one-bit black and white so a mixed set of speaker photos becomes one consistent texture.
Skip the big headline: put the practical facts in three quiet columns and let a full-bleed generative band carry the scale.
